probe: Prototype of check 7: a host-state scan with a deny list built from this host at scan time
method: Throwaway scanner in the scratchpad, standard library only. Host literals: home path, user name in a path, short hostname, repository absolute path and its sha256[:16], the Claude Code project-directory slug, user-scope marketplaces and plugins from ~/.claude/plugins, the model in ~/.codex/config.toml, the model in ~/.claude/settings.json. Fixed patterns: temporary and Nix paths, a path ending in scratchpad/, UUIDs, plan and usage-limit vocabulary in English and Korean. Blobs outside upstream/ and commit messages. Output names rules and paths only; no host value is recorded here.

false_positives.cause: the two user-scope plugin names are common English words and match as substrings of unrelated text (a script name, a word in a spec)
case-insensitive 'plus Tier' in 'a fresh closed-stem table plus Tier-1-style stem lookup'
the era 98 concept names the vocabulary it bans
an elided placeholder path '.../scratchpad/p9/...' in the P9 record

recall_on_pre_rewrite_history.refs: the local backups of the history before each rewrite of 2026-09-18
caught: session UUIDs and the private artifact link
plan and usage-limit wording (14 files in English, 7 in Korean)

missed.cause: it was committed in home-relative form (~/...), the form the logger and the verifiers write; the rule matched only the absolute form

missed.item: a user-scope plugin, a user marketplace and the Claude Code model setting
missed.cause: host drift: all three have since been removed or changed on the host, so a deny list read from the current configuration no longer contains them
a fragment of a path; the file was flagged only through other rules
a date is not a rule; files were flagged through the wording around it

verdict: A host-derived deny list is feasible and fast. It must match the home-relative form of paths, match host words on word boundaries, and be backed by a local accumulated list, because host configuration drifts and past values disappear from it. Vocabulary rules need case sensitivity and an allowlist for documents that discuss the rules.
